films.title: WHAT EVEN IS OMERTÀ? — Four players, one problem
films.concept: Four full-size criminals cannot get a gigantic polygon key around a concrete stairwell. The Rookie expected a quick mafia-game action. A stripped car becomes materials; earned knowledge makes a key craftable; four distinct people contribute; a human boss approves; the archive opens for the world. Smash-cut ELSEWHERE to a diverted shipment, a new market and an investigation. Phone fisheye, pavement inventory and industrial hardware make each new genre arrive as an interruption. The impossible prop is the joke; the requirements and consequences come from OMERTÀ.

thesis.recognition: Group raids, inventory grids, mafia hierarchy, phone coordination.
thesis.novelty: A gigantic key requires four full-size people and a real permission chain, then the city changes genre.
thesis.sensation: Stairwell clang → pavement inventory → hydraulic press → four simultaneous calls → city shutter.
thesis.patternInterrupt: Giant polygon key jammed at stairwell corner, FOUR adult carriers visible immediately.
thesis.informationGap: Why are other people and intel necessary for a door? The viewer learns the contributions before seeing the persistent payoff.
thesis.shareTrigger: The friend who turns one quick quest into a raid group.

films.claimNote: F01–F09, F12–F17, F20–F23, F26–F27. Four seats are from the Foundry pilot, not every mission. “Elsewhere” at 21.0 explicitly separates the campaign example from the archive. The shipment is diverted through an authorized operation; it is not a randomly disappearing commodity. Full-release master under L01 and L05; all pictured systems are available at publication.

films.title: THE ECONOMY IS THE GAME — Your Family is on the chart
films.concept: A Rookie buys bulk cargo and ends up behind a tower of hard cases on a freight scale. Pickup becomes convoy, partial loss, a rival dock toll and Family cash. A full-size exchange pit interrupts: game cash is separate from OMR. Her canonical OMR sale brings in the Hook and POL/Core; a separate seasonal Turf lane becomes a rooftop territorial contest. She then gestures at an actual swimming pool while the Auditor explains that Family rights concern eligible funded fees and protocol principal stays protocol-owned. The exchange, rooftop and swimming pool are deliberately jarring editorial metaphors tied to precise game relationships.

thesis.recognition: Delivery disasters, guild turf, exchange terminals, crypto liquidity, literal pool joke.
thesis.novelty: A cargo pickup becomes a separate OMR/Hook system and a rooftop fight over prospective fee rights.
thesis.sensation: Freight beep → axle-cam theft → wire-fence payment → exchange pit → rooftop court → swimming pool.
thesis.patternInterrupt: Freight flash: Rookie nearly buried behind hard cases on industrial scale.
thesis.informationGap: Why does one cargo purchase end with a Family fighting over a section of a market chart?
thesis.shareTrigger: The friend who will argue over what holding a liquidity territory actually owns.

films.claimNote: Full-release master under L01–L03 and L05. F10–F11, F24, F29, F32, F35–F38 and F42 apply. The Rookie owns the collected bulk cargo before dispatch; the staged ambush leaves a verified remainder. The destination is another Family’s territory, with the shipper present and funded for a positive toll. The canonical OMR sale is a separate human-confirmed action, not an automatic result of cargo trading. Hook POL funding goes to Core; designated seasonal Turf LP fees go through their own bridge. A siege settlement changes prospective rights, not historical credits or principal ownership. No tokenomics numbers, projected yield or invented receipt.

Consigliere: Clear older female voice, dry, lightly telephone-filtered; no robotic vocoder. Auditor: Precise mid-register female voice; short attacks and impatient breaths.

films.title: THE GAME IS WATCHING YOU — The leak was outside
films.concept: The Don demands a rat in an ugly ultra-wide phone call. His AI adviser points him toward a giant public shipping notice. Tabloid photos crash into a fluorescent copyshop, independent source checks and an opaque city window that refuses the viewer private information. Two players contribute through separate terminals, the Don approves and the authorized Auditor executes. A city lightbox carries the persistent result. The adviser is a dry human-form call persona, and the joke is that everyone wants a verdict while the game only supports a recorded disclosure.

thesis.recognition: Tabloid accusations, video calls, screenshot arguments, private windows, investigation games.
thesis.novelty: The AI adviser is the only person refusing to turn a public notice into a guilty verdict.
thesis.sensation: Phone distortion → huge public notice → fluorescent paper snap → deny tone → city lightbox.
thesis.patternInterrupt: Ugly ultra-wide Don phone face: “Find the rat.” Blank phone fills lower foreground.
thesis.informationGap: Why is the suspected leak public, and why can two matching records still fail to establish guilt?
thesis.shareTrigger: The friend who mistakes two screenshots for two sources; the adviser says no.
